_readme: Sourcing ledger for app/public/people/*.webp, promised by docs/AVATARS.md ('The prompts are kept with each Higgsfield job and repeated in app/public/people/manifest.json once the images are brought into the repository.') but never created.

Each key is the stable person id (the filename stem before -64/-128/-256/-512). kind is 'generated' (Higgsfield, project 'CyberJudah People Avatars', workspace 28f5ce8d-ddb7-41e6-b137-a3c55b619076) or 'archival' (a real public-domain work, not generated).

status 'approved' / 'awaiting_review' is copied verbatim from docs/AVATARS.md, not re-judged here. status 'needs_confirmation' or 'documented_but_not_hosted' marks a gap this seat found but could not close without inventing data (rule 3, ops/RULES.md): see note.

This file currently covers only the ids docs/AVATARS.md documents with enough detail to record without guessing. The live app/public/people/ directory holds well over 150 further ids (ordinary avatars from Batches 2-3 onward, and the People portraits reused onto Timeline events) with no job id recorded anywhere in the repo yet. Their generation jobs do exist and are readable from the Higgsfield project's history (confirmed by this seat, 2026-10-06), but matching each live .webp to its correct job record needs a visual/hash match against that history, batch by batch -- tracked as follow-up work, not done here to avoid mis-attributing the wrong job to the wrong file.

CYB-209 batch 2: the entries below (abel-gen-4-2 through ahiezer-num-1-12) were matched by paging the full Higgsfield 'CyberJudah People Avatars' generation history (about 700 completed jobs, 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-05) via show_generations, then for every id with more than one candidate job sharing the same subject/tribe/period prompt, downloading both the live .webp and each candidate's render and visually comparing pose, garment and complexion before recording a job id -- never picking by recency or filename alone (see each entry's note for the comparison outcome). alphaeus-mat-10-3 is flagged rather than guessed: no completed job for Alphaeus was found anywhere in that history.

CYB-209 batch 3: the entries below (amaziah-2ki-12-21 through bichri-2sa-20-1) were matched the same way as batch 2 -- paging the full Higgsfield 'CyberJudah People Avatars' generation history (about 550 completed image jobs found end-to-end in this pass, 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-05, immediately preceded by an unrelated children's-book project's jobs) via show_generations, then for every id with more than one candidate job sharing the same subject prompt, downloading both the live .webp and each candidate's render and visually comparing pose, crown/garment and complexion before recording a job id -- never picking by recency or filename alone (see each entry's note). balak-num-22-2 had six candidate jobs sharing a near-identical prompt (as flagged going into this batch); the live file turned out to match one of them almost pixel-for-pixel once compared at full resolution, so it was picked with high confidence rather than by recency. bela-gen-46-21 had two extra candidate jobs for a different Bela (an Edomite king, Genesis 36:32) that do not match this id's subject (Bela son of Benjamin, Genesis 46:21) at all; not recorded here, same pattern as the ahaziah entry in batch 2. All 18 ids in this batch were matched to a job; none needed to be flagged as unmatchable.
